decisions.reason: The adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display remains tightly anchored in the firm's core POS display business and still fits its service-led, problem-solving offer despite normal portfolio refresh risk.
The pegboard-back cardboard display is still a relevant variant within the firm's established shelf-display range and supports customer choice without stretching capabilities.
The eighth-pallet format continues to complement the firm's standard cardboard display portfolio for different retail footprints and is therefore worth retaining.
The wooden display pallet sits further from the firm's paper-based core and is more likely to be discontinued so resources can be focused on stronger cardboard display lines and new development.
The media-focused quarter-pallet display is comparatively niche and less attractive for continued support than broader, more reusable display concepts in the firm's main market.
